core: common escape sequences and Unicode escapes

claims.claim: Python strings can be indexed, with the first character at index 0; a one-character string is used where learners might expect a separate character type.
A slice selects a substring using a start boundary that is included and a stop boundary that is excluded; omitted bounds default to the start or end of the string.
Strings are immutable, so assigning to an indexed position is an error; making changed text produces a different string value instead.
The language reference defines string literals, escape sequences, and formatted string literals (f-strings), whose replacement fields contain expressions.
Python lexical analysis works on Unicode text and permits Unicode escape forms in string literals; the lesson uses a named Unicode escape as a small executable example.
Out-of-range individual string indexing raises an error, while an out-of-range slice is handled by the slice rules.
